News / TradingView / XAUUSD: Gold Breaks Below $3,800, Hits Lowest Level Since September 2025

XAUUSD: Gold Breaks Below $3,800, Hits Lowest Level Since September 2025 1 min read

XAUUSD Key points: Gold prices slide to $3,760 US dollar rallies across FX Bullion down 33% from peak

XAUUSD, D1, TradingView Stronger dollar and expectations of further Fed tightening deepen bullion’s retreat, with Wednesday’s meeting minutes offering the next policy test. 📉 Gold’s slide breaks another threshold Gold XAUUSD fell below $3,800 an ounce Wednesday, extending its retreat to the lowest level since September 2025. Spot prices dropped 1.6% to $3,760 in Asian trading, while December futures fell 1.9% to $3,789.40. The latest decline extends a substantial reversal from January’s record. Gold has shed nearly 33% from its $5,594.82 peak to float at current market prices. Wednesday’s fresh lows further sour the sentiment, leaving bullion on course for its worst calendar year since 2015. Elsewhere in metals land, silver dropped 3% toward $46 an ounce, while platinum and palladium also weakened. That breadth suggests the pressure extends beyond gold’s individual chart, with the dollar and interest-rate outlook weighing on the wider metals complex. 💵 The dollar keeps the pressure on The dollar remains near a 19-month high , supported by US economic data and Federal Reserve commentary favoring further tightening. A stronger greenback makes dollar-priced gold more expensive for overseas buyers, adding another obstacle to demand while bullion struggles to attract sustained buying interest. Higher yields also raise the cost of holding gold. Bullion pays no interest, making income-producing assets more competitive when borrowing costs rise. Markets priced a 96% probability of a quarter-point December Fed hike, with a small remaining chance of a larger half-point increase. Equity-market stress has provided limited protection. Analysts cited by Reuters said investors seeking cash can sell bullion to cover volatility elsewhere. 🏦 Fed minutes bring the next test Wednesday’s Fed minutes will offer more detail on October’s policy discussion. Traders will assess the strength of support for further tightening. The document is backward-looking, however, and predates the latest employment and inflation reports that strengthened expectations of a December increase. Recent economic releases have offered little relief. October retail sales rose 0.2%, while import prices increased 1.1%, above expectations. Continued spending alongside higher import costs complicates the inflation outlook, giving traders another reason to question how quickly monetary conditions might become more supportive for precious metals.

item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / Elon Musk Had a Facepalm Moment After Sean Duffy Defends Rejecting Free Starlink for FAA: ‘Our Airspace Is Very Big’

Elon Musk Had a Facepalm Moment After Sean Duffy Defends Rejecting Free Starlink for FAA: ‘Our Airspace Is Very Big’ 2 min read

SPCX LHX On Tuesday, Space Exploration Technologies Corp. SPCX CEO Elon Musk appeared to take a swipe at Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy after he defended the Federal Aviation Administration’s decision to turn down free Starlink terminals. Sean Duffy Explains Why FAA Rejected Free Starlink Musk reacted with a facepalm emoji to a video of Duffy explaining why the agency opted for a ground-based communications network instead of relying on Starlink.

Elon Musk @elonmusk

🤦‍♂️ https://t.co/DLC14CvtLT

Nov 17, 2026

Speaking about Musk’s offer, Duffy acknowledged Starlink’s capabilities but said the FAA needed a network that could serve its extensive nationwide infrastructure. “We thought that the best method is to have a network that’s based on the ground,” Duffy said. He also praised Starlink’s speed, calling its capabilities “remarkable,” but argued that the FAA has assets spread across a vast airspace that require a different approach. Duffy said the agency had previously evaluated an earlier version of Starlink at its technology laboratory, where officials encountered technical issues that needed addressing. However, he stated that the FAA has used Starlink for certain assets in Alaska and described the satellite service as a useful solution for specific applications.

Eric Daugherty @EricLDaugh

🚨 JUST IN: Sec. Sean Duffy RESPONDS to Elon Musk saying he offered the Trump admin FREE Starlink for the FAA, but was turned down "We thought that the best method is to have a network [that's] based on the ground." "What he's doing with Starlink and the speed is remarkable —… pic.twitter.com/4rL5ji95xr

Nov 17, 2026

Musk’s Starlink Offer Resurfaces After FAA Outage The exchange comes after Musk said Monday that he had offered free Starlink terminals to the FAA, but Duffy declined the proposal. “Free Starlinks for the FAA were offered to Sec. Duffy, but he said they were not needed. As it turns out, they were,” Musk wrote on X. The FAA temporarily halted departures nationwide on Nov. 13 after communications problems affected multiple air traffic control centers, disrupting more than thousands of flights. Officials attributed the disruption partly to a router failure during maintenance work on the agency’s telecommunications network. Duffy said the issue appeared connected to equipment installed by FAA contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. LHX , though the precise cause remained under investigation. The routers being replaced were approximately 25 years old, Duffy said, adding that they should have been replaced in 2006 . The FAA confirmed in 2025 that it was testing Starlink terminals, although Duffy has maintained that the satellite network would be “part of the solution” rather than a replacement for existing infrastructure. Price Action: On Tuesday, SpaceX shares closed up 3.16% at $141.70 and gained 1.19% in after-hours trading to $143.39, according to Benzinga Pro. Benzinga Edge Stock Rankings indicate that SpaceX has bearish price trends across the short, medium and long term. Kevin O’Leary Says Nvidia Needs Leader Who Can Manage ‘International Pressure’ as Crypto Punters Raise Odds of NVDA Stock Hitting $180 By Month-End 1 min read

NVDA Celebrity investor Kevin O’Leary on Tuesday endorsed NVIDIA Corp. NVDA interim CEO Colette Kress as the right leader to guide the chipmaker through its post- Jensen Huang transition. ‘The Company Has a Strong Bench’ O’Leary shared a clip on X from his Yahoo Finance interview, in which he argued that Nvidia should avoid a “splashy” external CEO hire. “What it needs now is a leader who can manage the scrutiny and international pressure,” the "Shark Tank" star said. “Colette knows the business. I’d give her a few quarters to lead and see how she does.” O’Leary voiced confidence in the semiconductor giant, emphasizing the strength of its internal engineering team in designing next-generation chips.

Kevin O'Leary aka Mr. Wonderful @kevinolearytv

I don’t think Nvidia needs a splashy outside hire. The company has a strong bench, with engineers already building its next generations of chips. What it needs now is a leader who can manage the scrutiny and international pressure. Colette knows the business. I’d give her a few… pic.twitter.com/CHebUldInv

Nov 17, 2026

O’Leary Rules Out Huang’s Comeback At the same time, O’Leary dismissed the possibility of Huang returning as CEO, citing heightened scrutiny over the Nvidia founder’s alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia’s board has also ruled out the possibility , with Board Chairman Harvey Jones saying Huang’s personal behavior was inconsistent with its code of conduct, standards and cultural norms. Interestingly, Huang said he would return as CEO if the board asked him. Crypto Bros Wager on NVDA Price Nvidia exceeded revenue and earnings expectations in the third quarter and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook for the fourth quarter. Punters on Polygon  (CRYPTO:   POL )-based  Polymarket nudged up the odds that NVDA would close the month above $180 to 22%, while the probability of a close above $160 held at 50%.

Price Action : NVIDIA shares rose 4.82% in after-hours trading, according to Benzinga Pro. The stock closed 0.44% lower at $155.46 during Tuesday’s regular trading session. Benzinga’s Edge Stock Rankings indicate that NVDA maintains a weaker price trend over the short, medium, and long terms. Post reports earnings tomorrow: What to expect 1 min read

POST

Packaged foods company Post POST will be announcing earnings results this Thursday after market hours. Here’s what to look for. Post missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $1.95 billion, down 1.8% year on year. It was a softer quarter for the company, with a miss of analysts’ EBITDA estimates. Is Post a buy or sell going into earnings? Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members . This quarter, the market is expecting Post’s revenue to decline 11.1% year on year, a reversal from the 11.8% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Post has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years. Looking at Post’s peers in the shelf-stable food segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. B&G Foods delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 4.7%, beating analysts’ expectations by 6.3%, and Hershey reported revenues up 3%, topping estimates by 0.8%. B&G Foods traded up 38% following the results while Hershey was also up 1.1%. Read our full analysis of B&G Foods’s results here and Hershey’s results here . There has been positive sentiment among investors in the shelf-stable food segment, with share prices up 4.2% on average over the last month. Post is up 6% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $96.67 (compared to the current share price of $82.05). item.content:encoded:
News / Cointelegraph / Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore

Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore Less than 1 min read

SOLUSD USDTUSD USDTUSD Two Ledger owners have reported cryptocurrency thefts involving hardware wallets they say were purchased from an authorized retailer in Dubai, raising concerns that a hardware wallet tampering campaign had also spread to the UAE. An X user posting as Rewinsky on Monday said they found their Ledger Flex had been tampered with after reporting the loss of about 1,300 Solana SOLUSD . Mark Karpelès’ Ledger Implant OSINT registry subsequently confirmed the device as containing a hardware implant.

The photo shows the same kind of antenna as seen in other Ledger Flex implants, according to Mark Karpeles. Source: Ledger Implant OSINT A second owner, posting as New Babylon Order Worldwide, said Tuesday that 507,000 USDt USDTUSD was stolen from their Ledger Stax on Saturday. They said the device was bought new at Virgin Megastore Dubai on Oct. 11, two days after Ledger publicly disclosed an investigation into crypto losses involving devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. The reports suggest the Ledger device tampering has extended past retailers in just Asia and Europe. Ledger lists Virgin Megastores among its authorized retailers in the United Arab Emirates. Virgin Megastore lists eight stores in Dubai, including branches at Dubai Mall, Mall of the Emirates and Dubai Hills Mall. Cointelegraph reached out to Ledger and Virgin Megastore for comment.
